policies.summary: For a permit by rule, a project that would disturb more than 10 acres of prime agricultural soils or 50 acres of contiguous forest (or any enrolled forestry preservation land) is deemed to have a significant adverse impact and must submit a mitigation plan with a 45-day public comment period.

policies.state_body: Virginia Department of Environmental Quality (permit by rule, projects up to 150 MW); State Corporation Commission (larger projects and utility-owned projects)
policies.summary: Utility-scale projects need local land use approval unless the locality allows them by right (for ground-mounted solar of 1 MW or more, a special exception or siting agreement), and also a state approval. Wind, solar and battery projects up to 150 MW use a Department of Environmental Quality permit by rule, which requires the locality to certify land use compliance and applies to wind over 5 MW, solar over 5 MW that disturbs more than 10 acres, and storage that disturbs more than 10 acres. Larger plants, and plants of utilities whose rates the Commission sets, need a State Corporation Commission permit.

Unless a project is allowed by right, every locality must require a special exception (or a siting agreement) for ground-mounted solar of 1 MW or more and must write state criteria into its zoning ordinance: setbacks of 150 to 200 feet from non-participating dwellings, 50 to 100 feet from roads and 50 to 75 feet from non-participating property lines, panels no higher than 25 feet, screening, soil and decommissioning terms, with any variance only by agreement. A siting agreement may set less strict terms, localities need not approve, and each decision and the reason for any denial must be reported to the State Corporation Commission.

restrictions.description: Comprehensive plan update limits solar projects to 200 acres in urban areas and prohibits new projects within 2 miles of existing ones.
restrictions.long_description: In July 2021, the Augusta County Board of Supervisors updated the Utilities section of the County’s Comprehensive Plan to establish policies that would limit the size of industrial solar facilities. The update provided that solar farms are strongly discouraged from using more than 200 acres of land and that they should not be built in Urban Service and Community Development areas. In December 2023, Augusta County prohibited new solar projects in urban service and community development areas; at the same time, Augusta mandated that new solar projects must be located at least 2 miles from existing solar projects.

restrictions.long_description: In June 2024 the Board of Supervisors voted unanimously in favor of amendments to the county’s Comprehensive Plan and Zoning Ordinance to regulate renewable energy facilities. The amendments define utility-scale solar projects as those with a capacity of 1 MW or greater and limit the total size of any such projects to 500 acres. The amendments further require that such projects be set back at least 1 mile from any town or city boundary and at least 2 miles from any existing solar project. Further, any solar projects interconnecting to the grid must be located within 2 miles of transmission line corridors.

projects.description: In 2016, Longroad Energy proposed a 105-MW solar project to be located on approximately 799 acres near Chase City.
projects.long_description: In 2016, Longroad Energy proposed a 105-MW solar project to be located on approximately 799 acres near Chase City. In September 2021, the Mecklenburg County Planning Commission unanimously voted against permitting construction of the project as proposed, mainly because of the county’s 500-acre maximum for solar projects. In response, the developer scaled down the project to 80 MW on 500 acres, expanded setbacks from 150 feet to 250 feet (or more), and proactively coordinated with the Virginia Departments of Environmental Quality and Wildlife Resources to add wider buffers from aquatic resources. In August 2024, the Board of Supervisors voted 7 to 2 to reject the developer’s proposed siting agreement despite its pledge to donate $500,000 to Chase City in addition to the anticipated financial benefits to the county

projects.description: In December 2022, the County Planning Commission rejected an application for a 90-MW solar farm on private land.
projects.long_description: In December 2022, the County Planning Commission rejected an application for a 90-MW solar farm on private land. The project would be developed across 1,000 acres, including approximately 489 acres of prime farmland. In January 2023, the Mecklenburg County Board of Supervisors similarly rejected the application for the project. In reaching their decision, the Board cited the loss of 489 acres of prime farmland as a chief concern. The majority of the local residents in attendance at the Board’s public meeting, including the former County Clerk, spoke against the project raising concerns about potential contamination of nearby creeks and groundwater, impacts on wildlife, and land. On February 8, 2023, the developer, RWE Renewables Americas, LLC, filed a lawsuit challenging the Board’s decision. The lawsuit remains pending in the Mecklenburg Circuit Court. In April 2025, the developer submitted a revised project proposal for review by the County Planning Commission. The revised proposal provided that only 220 acres of prime farmland would be dedicated to the project and more than half of the total 1,000 acres of leased land would be placed in a conservation easement. The Commission rejected the project for a second time, concluding that it was not in compliance with the county plan because it “would destroy prime farmland and threaten the nearby watershed.”

projects.description: In November 2021, the Henry County Board of Zoning Appeals rejected Axton Solar LLC’s request to add 484 acres to a previously approved 1,203-acre solar project on agricultural land in the unincorporated community of Axton.
projects.long_description: In November 2021, the Henry County Board of Zoning Appeals rejected Axton Solar LLC’s request to add 484 acres to a previously approved 1,203-acre solar project on agricultural land in the unincorporated community of Axton. The request was denied due to concerns about aesthetic impacts and an ordinance that mandates that no more than 2.5% of the land area within a 5-mile radius may be used by solar. In December 2022, after the developer reduced the total project size to about 1,000 acres, with only 434 acres covered in panels, the Henry County Board of Zoning Appeals approved the project. However, on April 25, 2023, the Henry County Board of Supervisors rejected the project on finding that it would exceed the 2.5% cap by 93 acres.

projects.description: In October 2023, the Prince George County Planning Commission determined that RWE Clean Energy’s proposed 100-MW, 505-acre solar farm was not in substantial accord with the county’s comprehensive plan, as it would exceed the county’s limit for the size of a solar farm.
projects.long_description: In October 2023, the Prince George County Planning Commission determined that RWE Clean Energy’s proposed 100-MW, 505-acre solar farm was not in substantial accord with the county’s comprehensive plan, as it would exceed the county’s limit for the size of a solar farm. Some residents have opposed the project, expressing concerns about impacts to farming and hunting.

projects.description: In April 2021, Fauquier County planning officials rejected an application for a 40-acre solar farm in Bealeton.
projects.long_description: In April 2021, Fauquier County planning officials rejected an application for a 40-acre solar farm in Bealeton. This application was the first to be considered since Fauquier County passed a restrictive solar development ordinance in October of 2020. Officials rejected the application because the project would have been located on prime farmland, which they claimed was incompatible with the County’s comprehensive plan.

projects.description: A 5,000-acre, 600-MW solar farm proposed by Blackwater Solar LLC has sparked significant objections from local residents.
projects.long_description: A 5,000-acre, 600-MW solar farm proposed by Blackwater Solar LLC has sparked significant objections from local residents. In May 2023, the developer began the application process for a conditional use permit for the project. In March 2024, the Sussex County Board of Supervisors and Planning Commission heard opinions on the project at a public meeting attended by over 300 people, with many opponents raising concerns about erosion, loss of woodlands, damage to wetlands, contamination of runoff, and the risk of battery fires. On June 3, 2024, the Board of Supervisors voted to deny the permits.

projects.description: The 100-acre Cape Solar project was first proposed in 2018.
projects.long_description: The 100-acre Cape Solar project was first proposed in 2018. The project faced intense opposition from Page County Citizens for Responsible Solar, and the Page County Board of Supervisors denied the application. The developer submitted a new application in December 2020. However, in March 2022, the Page County Planning Commission recommended denial of the revised application due to the anticipated loss of agricultural land, visual impacts, and environmental impacts. In June 2022, the Page County Board of Supervisors adopted a restrictive ordinance that limited projects to 30 acres. On August 16, 2022, the developer withdrew the application.

projects.description: In February 2019, Cypress Creek Renewables withdrew its application for a solar project after the Powhatan County Planning Commission recommended denial of the application and the Board of Supervisor denied an appeal of the Planning Commission’s decision to recommend denial.
projects.long_description: In February 2019, Cypress Creek Renewables withdrew its application for a solar project after the Powhatan County Planning Commission recommended denial of the application and the Board of Supervisor denied an appeal of the Planning Commission’s decision to recommend denial. The project faced intense local opposition in the community.

projects.municipality: Town of Windsor, Village of Zuni
projects.description: On February 23, 2023, the Isle of Wight County Supervisors rejected an application for a 71-MW, 637-acre solar farm between the Village of Zuni and the Town of Windsor.
projects.long_description: On February 23, 2023, the Isle of Wight County Supervisors rejected an application for a 71-MW, 637-acre solar farm between the Village of Zuni and the Town of Windsor. Immediately prior to the vote, opponents spoke out against the project, citing visual impacts of the project and concerns about electromagnetic fields. Five days after the vote, the count planning commission voted to recommend that the county supervisors establish a cap on the cumulative acreage of solar farms at 2% of the county’s prime farmlands.

projects.project_name: Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind Project (City of Virginia Beach)
projects.description: In 2020, Dominion Energy proposed the Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind Project, a 2,600-MW offshore wind farm.
projects.long_description: In 2020, Dominion Energy proposed the Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind Project, a 2,600-MW offshore wind farm. In March 2024, the Committee for a Constructive Tomorrow, Heartland Institute, and National Legal and Policy Center filed a lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia to halt the project. The lawsuit alleged that the construction would threaten the endangered North Atlantic right whale and that Dominion had not taken sufficient steps to protect right whales. The lawsuit further alleged that, when it approved the project, the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) failed to consider the cumulative impacts of offshore wind farms on the right whale population in violation of the Endangered Species Act. The plaintiffs moved for a preliminary injunction to halt the project’s construction until the National Marine Fisheries Service issues a new biological opinion. In May 2024, the court denied the request for preliminary injunction, stating that the plaintiffs failed to demonstrate that they would suffer irreparable harm and to account for the extensive measures to protect whales already in place. Separately, residents of Virginia Beach have raised concerns about vibrations, scenic disruptions, and environmental harm from the Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind Project. Dominion has stated that it has provided multiple opportunities for residents to engage with the company and that it is implementing measures to address their concerns. On December 22, 2025, the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) issued a stop-work order to halt the construction of the project for reasons of national security. The next day, on December 23, 2025, the developer filed a lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia to enjoin BOEM’s stop-work order. In January 2026, the federal district judge granted the plaintiff’s request for a preliminary injunction and allowed construction of the project to resume.

projects.description: On March 14, 2023, the Halifax Town Council rejected a request to rezone 86 acres from residential to manufacturing to allow for construction of the 5-MW Crawford Road Solar project.
projects.long_description: On March 14, 2023, the Halifax Town Council rejected a request to rezone 86 acres from residential to manufacturing to allow for construction of the 5-MW Crawford Road Solar project. The decision followed a public hearing in which opponents raised concerns about impacts on property values and visual impacts. More than 100 town residents purportedly signed a petition opposing the project.

projects.description: The proposed 1,600-acre Cricket Solar project faced concerted opposition from Citizens for Responsible Solar.
projects.long_description: The proposed 1,600-acre Cricket Solar project faced concerted opposition from Citizens for Responsible Solar. The opponents’ arguments focused, in large part, on stormwater runoff, wetlands impacts, and the proximity of Civil War battle sites. The developer revised its application to address these concerns. However, in the face of continued opposition, the developer withdrew the revised application in August 2019.

projects.description: In March 2024, the Orange County Board of Supervisors unanimously rejected plans for a 17-acre community solar project proposed by RWE Clean Energy, after the planning commission had previously recommended approval.
projects.long_description: In March 2024, the Orange County Board of Supervisors unanimously rejected plans for a 17-acre community solar project proposed by RWE Clean Energy, after the planning commission had previously recommended approval. In voting to deny the project, supervisors raised concerns about visual impacts.

projects.description: In September 2023, the Halifax County Planning Commission recommended that a permit for the 102-MW Hillendale Solar project be denied.
projects.long_description: In September 2023, the Halifax County Planning Commission recommended that a permit for the 102-MW Hillendale Solar project be denied. One of the planning commissioners stated that the project would not be a good fit with initiatives meant to preserve the nearby Staunton River. Residents voiced both support and opposition to the project, with some residents questioning the environmental impacts of solar energy.

projects.description: In March 2023, the James City County Board of Supervisors rejected Pivot Energy’s application to develop a 4.75-MW solar farm.
projects.long_description: In March 2023, the James City County Board of Supervisors rejected Pivot Energy’s application to develop a 4.75-MW solar farm. Opposition to the project—including from the Colonial Soil and Water Conservation District—had centered on impacts to prime farmland. The James City County Planning Commission had recommended approval of the project in November 2022.

projects.project_name: Kitty Hawk Wind Project Cable Landing (City of Virginia Beach)
projects.description: The Kitty Hawk Wind Project, a 3,500-MW offshore wind farm proposed by Avangrid Renewables, has encountered significant community resistance around the proposed site of a cable landing.
projects.long_description: The Kitty Hawk Wind Project, a 3,500-MW offshore wind farm proposed by Avangrid Renewables, has encountered significant community resistance around the proposed site of a cable landing. In 2017, the company secured the rights to develop a lease area off the coast of the Outer Banks. The neighborhood of Sandbridge in Virginia Beach was selected as the site for the project’s cable landing. In November 2023, the City Manager and Mayor informed the developer that the city could not support the landing due to the amount of community pushback. Local opponents include an organization called Protect Sandbridge Beach Coalition, which has met with City Council members and sought an independent assessment of the landing. Opponents have expressed concerns about potential economic impacts, including tourism and property value impacts; environmental impacts, including hindrances on efforts to renourish beaches; and construction-related noise disruptions and road blockages. Many of the opponents claim that they do not oppose offshore wind farms in general but object to the site selection for the landing. In March 2024, the developer provided a new economic impact report to the Council, emphasizing the benefits of the project. As of December 31, 2024, the City had not made a decision to approve the cable landing.

projects.description: In October 2021, the Dinwiddie County Board of Supervisors voted against a rezoning agreement that would have allowed for the Lily Pond Solar project to be built.
projects.long_description: In October 2021, the Dinwiddie County Board of Supervisors voted against a rezoning agreement that would have allowed for the Lily Pond Solar project to be built. This 80-MW project would have spanned 600 acres of land.

projects.description: In September 2023, Mecklenburg County commissioners voted against a small-scale agrivoltaic project proposed by RC Revco.
projects.long_description: In September 2023, Mecklenburg County commissioners voted against a small-scale agrivoltaic project proposed by RC Revco. The project would have shared land with sheep grazing and pollinator plants. However, despite testimony about the symbiotic relationship between the land uses, commissioners expressed skepticism as to the viability of the shared use of land.

projects.description: In 2020, Strata Clean Energy submitted an application for the 149-MW Maroon Solar project but withdrew the application after intense pushback from neighbors and Citizens for Responsible Solar.
projects.long_description: In 2020, Strata Clean Energy submitted an application for the 149-MW Maroon Solar project but withdrew the application after intense pushback from neighbors and Citizens for Responsible Solar. In 2021, the Culpeper County Board of Supervisors denied a second application for the project. In 2022, Strata submitted a third application. However, in January 2023, the planning commission recommended denial of the project because it was in conflict with the county’s policy of limiting projects to 300 acres; the Maroon Solar project would span across 1,800 acres of agricultural land and include 671 acres of panels. On February 7, 2023, the board of supervisors codified that policy by adopting an ordinance that limited projects to 300 acres. One week later, the developer withdrew its third application for the project.

projects.description: In August 2022, the Greensville County Board of Supervisors unanimously denied an application for the proposed Monarch Solar Project, which would have generated 123 MW on 700 acres of land.
projects.long_description: In August 2022, the Greensville County Board of Supervisors unanimously denied an application for the proposed Monarch Solar Project, which would have generated 123 MW on 700 acres of land. In rejecting the project, the Board decided that the project was not in substantial accord with the Greensville County Comprehensive Plan, overturning the Planning Commission’s prior determination.

projects.project_name: Mountain Pine Arvonia I and II
projects.description: Hodson Energy is seeking to develop an 80-MW solar project on 1,065 acres in Buckingham County.
projects.long_description: Hodson Energy is seeking to develop an 80-MW solar project on 1,065 acres in Buckingham County. In November 2023, following a presentation about two potential 80-MW solar arrays, Buckingham residents expressed opposition to the projects. At the opponents’ urging, county commissioners agreed to pause consideration of solar projects until the board of supervisors approved a draft solar ordinance. In February 2024, Buckingham County supervisors approved the project, with conditions including 400-foot residential setbacks and 75-foot wetland setbacks. The project still required state approval before proceeding.

projects.description: In September 2023, Mecklenburg County commissioners voted against a small-scale agrivoltaic project proposed by RC Revco at the same commissioner meeting in which they voted against the Lone Oak Agrisolar Project.
projects.long_description: In September 2023, Mecklenburg County commissioners voted against a small-scale agrivoltaic project proposed by RC Revco at the same commissioner meeting in which they voted against the Lone Oak Agrisolar Project. The New Hope project would have shared land with tobacco farming, but the commissioners expressed skepticism as to the feasibility of dual use.

projects.description: Strata Clean Energy proposed a 72-MW solar development on approximately 1,500 acres of privately owned land in the Beaverdam District adjacent to Caroline County and the North Anna River.
projects.long_description: Strata Clean Energy proposed a 72-MW solar development on approximately 1,500 acres of privately owned land in the Beaverdam District adjacent to Caroline County and the North Anna River. Approximately 340 acres would be covered by solar panels and 914 acres would be designated as a conservation area throughout the project’s 35-year lifespan. The project included plans to reforest parts of the Beaverdam development and provide 150-foot buffers around the site to dampen any potential sound. The developer held five meetings with the community between April and June of 2024 to address concerns about the size and scope of the project, including concerns over deforestation and the impact to local wildlife. On July 18, 2024, the Hanover County Planning Commission held a public meeting at which more than a dozen local residents opposed the project. The commission denied the application but forwarded the matter to the Board of Supervisors for a final decision. In September 2024, the Board unanimously rejected the project which would have been the largest solar farm in the county.

projects.description: In June 2023, the Culpeper County Planning Commission determined that North Ridge Culpeper Solar LLC’s application for a 26-MW, 355-acre solar project was not in compliance with the county’s comprehensive plan.
projects.long_description: In June 2023, the Culpeper County Planning Commission determined that North Ridge Culpeper Solar LLC’s application for a 26-MW, 355-acre solar project was not in compliance with the county’s comprehensive plan. The Board of Supervisors upheld this determination, after which the developer withdrew its application for a conditional use permit. The project had faced opposition from a local organization called Citizens for Responsible Solar, the leader of which had spoken against the project, citing its proximity to another nearby solar farm.

projects.description: The Old Ridge Road project was a planned 3-MW solar facility being developed by New Leaf Solar on 64 acres of land in Prince Edward County.
projects.long_description: The Old Ridge Road project was a planned 3-MW solar facility being developed by New Leaf Solar on 64 acres of land in Prince Edward County. In January 2024, following a public hearing on the project’s application for a special use permit, the local planning commission unanimously voted not to recommend the project for approval by the Prince Edward County Board of Supervisors. Local opponents at the public hearing had raised concerns that the facility would produce run-off, decrease local property values, and degrade environmental conditions. New Leaf Solar officially withdrew its application for a special use permit in March 2024.

projects.description: The Orange Road Solar Farm was a 5-MW, 22-acre community solar facility proposed by ESA Solar.
projects.long_description: The Orange Road Solar Farm was a 5-MW, 22-acre community solar facility proposed by ESA Solar. In February 2024, the Orange County Planning Commission voted 4-1 to recommend that the county’s Board of Supervisors deny a special use permit for the project. Leading up to the vote, the owners of Mayhurst—a historic estate that served as a bed and breakfast and wedding venue—leveraged social media to rally opposition to the project, based on concerns about impacts to tourism and agriculture. One commissioner cited the project’s proximity (1,000 feet) to Mayhurst as a basis for the decision to recommend project denial. In March 2024, ESA Solar withdrew its application for the project.

projects.description: Energix Renewables proposed a 50-MW solar facility on 180 acres in Amherst County.
projects.long_description: Energix Renewables proposed a 50-MW solar facility on 180 acres in Amherst County. In September 2023, the Amherst County Planning Commission voted against a permit for the 50-MW Piney River Solar Project—the second such vote against the Piney River Solar Project in six months. Some residents voiced opposition to the project on the basis of potential environmental impacts, while others have supported the project as a means to improve the environment. In February 2024, the Amherst County Board of Supervisors unanimously voted to deny a special exception permit for the project, finding that the project was not substantially in accord with Amherst County’s comprehensive plan for growth and development. According to the developer, the project would have provided an estimated $10 million in tax revenue over a lifespan of 45 years.

projects.description: Developer SolUnesco proposed an 800-MW solar project in Charlotte County.
projects.long_description: Developer SolUnesco proposed an 800-MW solar project in Charlotte County. A lawsuit filed on September 28, 2021 alleged that the developer improperly entered into a lease agreement with a landowner who had dementia, circumventing her power of attorney after her power of attorney had rejected the developer’s offer multiple times. In July 2022, the project received necessary permits. Approximately 4,500 acres will be fenced in, and approximately 3,000 acres will be covered with solar panels and other equipment.

projects.description: In November 2021, the Henry County Board of Zoning Appeals rejected Invenergy’s proposal for the 90-MW Rocky Ford Solar Energy Project at the same meeting as it rejected Axton Solar LLC’s request to add 484 acres to a previously approved project.
projects.long_description: In November 2021, the Henry County Board of Zoning Appeals rejected Invenergy’s proposal for the 90-MW Rocky Ford Solar Energy Project at the same meeting as it rejected Axton Solar LLC’s request to add 484 acres to a previously approved project. As with Axton Solar’s request, Invenergy’s application was denied due to concerns about aesthetic impacts and an ordinance that mandates that no more than 2.5% of the land area within a 5-mile radius may be used by solar. However, after the developer reduced the project size from 800 acres to 378 acres, the county approved the project.

projects.description: On January 26, 2016, the Botetourt County Board of Supervisors voted to permit Apex Clean Energy to construct a 25-turbine, 75-MW project on a mountain ridge in Southwest Virginia.
projects.long_description: On January 26, 2016, the Botetourt County Board of Supervisors voted to permit Apex Clean Energy to construct a 25-turbine, 75-MW project on a mountain ridge in Southwest Virginia. However, the project has faced local opposition and construction has been delayed repeatedly. On November 10, 2021, a group called Citizens for Responsible Energy, also known as Virginians for Responsible Energy, filed a lawsuit challenging the project. In 2022, the American Bird Conservancy submitted comments raising concerns about impacts to Golden Eagles. The lawsuit was dismissed in January 2024, and the dismissal was upheld on appeal in September 2024. As of September 2024, Apex was still waiting on a purchase agreement and site plan approval, with construction anticipated to begin in 2025 and to be completed in late 2026.

projects.description: In October 2023, the Halifax County Planning Commission postponed a hearing on the 5-MW South Boston Solar G Development amidst heavy local opposition.
projects.long_description: In October 2023, the Halifax County Planning Commission postponed a hearing on the 5-MW South Boston Solar G Development amidst heavy local opposition. In November 2023, the commission came to a split 3-3 vote on permitting the project, sending the matter to the Halifax County Board of Supervisors, which approved the project in December 2023.

projects.description: A local group called Concerned Citizens of Spotsylvania County spent several thousand dollars fighting proposed 6,350-acre Spotsylvania Solar Energy Center.
projects.long_description: A local group called Concerned Citizens of Spotsylvania County spent several thousand dollars fighting proposed 6,350-acre Spotsylvania Solar Energy Center. The opposition group was comprised largely of residents from the wealthy, gated Fawn Lake subdivision. The project ultimately received state and local approvals in 2018 and 2019, despite opposition.

projects.description: Developer BayWa proposed an 80-MW solar project on approximately 1,000 acres of privately-owned land near the border of Orange and Culpeper counties.
projects.long_description: Developer BayWa proposed an 80-MW solar project on approximately 1,000 acres of privately-owned land near the border of Orange and Culpeper counties. In June 2024, the Planning Commission unanimously voted to recommend denial of the proposal. The commission’s public meeting drew a large audience, with 22 local residents giving public comment, the majority in opposition to the project. The opponents spoke about traffic and safety concerns during construction, decommissioning plans, ecological impact, and the county’s rural character. In August 2024, the Board of Supervisors unanimously denied the special use permit upon finding that the project was not in accord with the county’s comprehensive plan. The project was the largest proposal in the county and was projected to generate more than $20 million in new revenue over 25 years, in addition to $2.3 million in wages and benefits and $10.3 million in economic output.

projects.description: In November 2023, the Fluvanna County Planning Commission decided to defer a proposal for a 38-MW solar farm on over 400 acres of land in Virginia.
projects.long_description: In November 2023, the Fluvanna County Planning Commission decided to defer a proposal for a 38-MW solar farm on over 400 acres of land in Virginia. Many residents had voiced their opposition to the project at a Commission meeting, expressing concerns about impacts on untouched woods, along with concerns about radiation.

projects.description: In 2022, Catalyst Energy Solar Farm proposed the 262-MW Wolf Hills Solar project to be located on 1,900 acres of land in Abingdon, some of which was zoned for agricultural use.
projects.long_description: In 2022, Catalyst Energy Solar Farm proposed the 262-MW Wolf Hills Solar project to be located on 1,900 acres of land in Abingdon, some of which was zoned for agricultural use. The county’s planning commission unanimously denied the developer’s special-exception permit at a public hearing held on June 24, 2024. During the five-hour hearing, with over 300 people in attendance, residents opposing the project repeatedly raised concerns of loss of farmland, despite the developer’s plan to use sheep to manage the vegetation. The developer withdrew its application a week after the commission’s denial of the permit.

projects.description: Energix Renewables proposed the 80-MW Gabriel Solar Project, which would include a 120-MW battery energy storage component on approximately 539 acres, by far the largest such project proposed in the county.
projects.long_description: Energix Renewables proposed the 80-MW Gabriel Solar Project, which would include a 120-MW battery energy storage component on approximately 539 acres, by far the largest such project proposed in the county. At a planning commission public hearing in December 2024, landowners who support the project spoke about the short- and long-term benefits of the project, including significant revenue for the county. Residents who opposed the project raised concerns primarily related to fire safety planning and training for local firefighters. In January 2025 the county planning commission recommended approval. In March 2025, the Board of Supervisors rejected the project in a 7-1 vote, citing fire safety concerns and inconsistencies in the application documents.

projects.description: In 2023, Open Road Renewables proposed the 90-MW Almeda Solar Grazing Center (also known as Almeda Solar I) which included an agrivoltaics component to be developed on approximately 941 acres of farmland spanning 14 parcels.
projects.long_description: In 2023, Open Road Renewables proposed the 90-MW Almeda Solar Grazing Center (also known as Almeda Solar I) which included an agrivoltaics component to be developed on approximately 941 acres of farmland spanning 14 parcels. In April 2023, the Fauquier County Planning Commission rejected the proposal on a 4-1 vote citing concerns over the project scale, potential to disrupt or destroy historic resources, and inconsistency with Fauquier’s agrarian character. In 2025, the developer re-submitted a modified version of the proposal for the project to be located on 3 separate parcels of land, plans for 200-foot setbacks with vegetation buffers as well as decommissioning plans. The project would occupy less than 0.4% of the county’s farmland and less than 0.25% of its rural lands and is expected to generate $20 million in local tax revenue. In February 2025, following a public hearing, the Commission unanimously rejected the proposal finding it to be inconsistent with the county’s comprehensive plan. The majority of public comments heard by the Commission were from opponents of the project, who argued that farmland was being targeted and that the project was incompatible with the character of the county, and questioned the developers claims about job creation.

projects.description: In 2025, KDC Solar submitted a request to the Middlesex Planning Commission for a Special Exception for a 20-MW solar energy facility it planned to build on approximately 77 acres in Deltaville.
projects.long_description: In 2025, KDC Solar submitted a request to the Middlesex Planning Commission for a Special Exception for a 20-MW solar energy facility it planned to build on approximately 77 acres in Deltaville. In April 2025, the Middlesex Planning Commission unanimously recommended denial of the request to the County Board of Supervisors, noting that the project was not in accord with the county’s comprehensive plan. Opponents of the project had garnered over 440 signatures on petition in opposition to the project. Over 100 local residents attended the April public meeting and the majority of those who spoke raised concerns about the project, including the potential for it to decrease property values, cause environmental hazards, and change the rural character of the area. In June 2025, following a four-hour public hearing, the Board of Supervisors’ vote was split, 2-2, and thus the motion to approve the Special Exception for the project failed.

projects.description: AES proposed the 240-MW Sycamore Cross Solar project to be located on approximately 1,070 acres of land in Isle of Wight and Surry Counties.
projects.long_description: AES proposed the 240-MW Sycamore Cross Solar project to be located on approximately 1,070 acres of land in Isle of Wight and Surry Counties. In September 2024, the Isle of Wight County Supervisors, in a 3-2 vote, approved the proposal. In February 2025, the Surry County Board of Supervisors unanimously rejected the proposal following oral comments in opposition by community advocates, who expressed concerns that the project would change the community’s farming character.

projects.description: In 2024, Sun Tribe proposed the 22 MW, 215 acre Caledon Solar Project on private land owned by State Senator Richard Stuart who is also the King George County attorney.
projects.long_description: In 2024, Sun Tribe proposed the 22 MW, 215 acre Caledon Solar Project on private land owned by State Senator Richard Stuart who is also the King George County attorney. Project opponents, primarily conservationists, have argued that construction of a commercial solar facility would violate a perpetual open-space conservation easement that covers the property held by the Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation (DCR). Nevertheless, in November 2025, the King George County Board of Supervisors unanimously approved the request for a special exception permit for the project, disregarding the County Planning Commission’s recommendation to deny it. In December 2025, the DCR approved an amendment to the conservation easement, allowing construction of the Project. Opponents allege that Sen. Stuart only received the DCR approval after interventions by political allies, including Governor Glenn Youngkin.
